name: Pet tag
description: A red plastic tag shaped like a bone, on a small split ring. A pet's name is printed on it.
notes: 38 by 22 mm and 2 mm thick with a white name panel and a silver split ring. The box against the reference's 1 mL counts the ring and the bone's notches. A per-item pet name has no content field yet.

name: Down pillow
description: A down pillow rolled tight and held by two webbing straps.
notes: Rolled for carrying, 400 mm long and 180 mm across; the ends show the rolled layers in cloth-white and cloth-cotton, with cloth-navy straps. Unrolling it to sleep on needs a placed-object field the item schema does not have yet, so it has no workstation. The size is a placeholder.

name: Electronic scrap
description: A handful of resistors, capacitors and diodes pulled from circuit boards.
notes: A loose heap about 40 by 26 mm: three banded resistors, a can capacitor, two ceramic disc capacitors and two diodes with clipped legs. The box against the reference's 5 mL counts the air in a loose heap. The light detector rides here as the brief has variants do, though a single photocell would read differently; give it its own model if it becomes a crafting part in its own right.

name: Heating element
description: A sheathed steel heating loop on a round mounting flange, from a kettle or a hot plate.
notes: A flat loop 90 mm across on two legs, a flange 50 mm across with a hex nut, a ceramic insulator and two brass terminal pins. The box against the reference's 250 mL counts the open middle of the loop.

name: Evaporator coil
description: Copper tubing bent back and forth through a stack of thin aluminium fins, from a refrigerator or air conditioner.
notes: 500 mm long, 300 mm tall and 60 mm deep: two banks of eight tubes joined by U bends outside galvanised end plates, with 23 fins and two stub pipes. CHECK VOLUME (x5.1): the reference's 2 L is far less than any coil this heavy occupies, and the box counts the air between fins and tubes. The reference names steel; copper tubes and aluminium fins are what such coils are made of, so the look follows them while the mass stays the reference's 20 kg. The size is a placeholder.

name: Desk fan
description: An electric desk fan with three blades inside a wire guard, on a round base.
notes: 420 mm tall with a guard 300 mm across, facing +z. The guards are stepped domes of rings and spokes. plastic-clear-blue draws the blades. Running it needs mains power, which has no content field yet, and it brings no crafting quality. The size is a placeholder.

name: Glowing egg
description: A hard, glassy egg the size of a plum. Faint light flickers among sharp shards inside it.
notes: Laid by a mutant spider-thing: a ball 46 mm across with a short drawn-out tip, shell in see-through gem-purple over a core of lcd-green shards. The tiles draw the shell opaque, so the shards show only in the game. It does not glow: no finish emits light, and a light source on an item has no content field yet. The box against the reference's 50 mL counts the air around a round egg. Its source creature does not exist in Deadvox yet.

name: Chitin strut
description: A stiff, ridged strut of chitin from inside a giant insect, forked at one end.
notes: 280 mm long: four jointed segments tapering from 22 mm across, a knob at the root, a two-pronged fork at the tip and a ridge along each segment, in leather-brown with resin-honey joints. The reference marks it for milling into powder; milling has no content field yet. Its source creature does not exist in Deadvox yet.

name: Evacuation records drive
description: A portable hard drive with a hand-written label. It holds evacuation plans, staff lists and the last messages copied from a disaster agency's servers.
notes: 118 by 80 by 18 mm with rounded long sides, a written label, a green status light and a short coiled cable. The agency is left unnamed. Reading the drive needs a computer and a readable-content field, neither of which exists yet.

name: Fire brick
description: A pale, light brick made to line kilns and fireplaces without cracking in the heat.
notes: A full insulating fire brick, 230 by 114 by 64 mm, in paperboard-tan with a scorched patch and a chipped corner; such bricks really weigh about the reference's 969 g at full size. The box against the reference's 500 mL is the full brick's 1.7 L. hammering 1 mirrors the reference's HAMMER quality. Building a forge or kiln lining from it has no content field yet.

name: Fishbowl
description: A round glass bowl of water over a bed of gravel, with a goldfish swimming in it.
notes: 260 mm across and 222 mm tall with a flared lip, about 7 L of water in plastic-clear-blue, stone-grey gravel and an orange fish. The tiles draw the glass opaque, so the fish shows only in the game. The mass includes the water, as liquids in their container do. A live fish, emptying the bowl and an empty-bowl state have no content fields yet; the empty bowl would get its own model.

name: Garnet
description: A loose cut garnet, deep red.
notes: A round brilliant 10 mm across lying on its table in gem-red; at the finest 2 mm grain a stone reads as a stepped red dome. It is drawn a little larger than the reference's 0.2 g, a stone of about 1 carat, so it is more than a single voxel. CHECK VOLUME (x0.10): the reference's 6 mL is a floor for tiny items, not the stone's size. Every gem shares this model, as jewellery shares one model across its gem versions; a per-variant finish (gem-purple for amethyst, gem-green for emerald and peridot, gem-blue for sapphire, aquamarine and topaz) has no field yet. Pearl, opal, malachite and onyx are cut round or as cabochons rather than faceted, so a cabochon model would suit them if a variant ever gets its own.

name: Tinted lenses
description: A pair of dark glass lenses from sunglasses.
notes: Two teardrop lenses 56 by 47 mm and 2 mm thick, mirrored and lying side by side, in glass-grey. CHECK VOLUME (x5.5): the reference's 2 mL is the glass alone; the box counts the outlines and the gap between the lenses. The tiles draw the glass opaque; it stays see-through in the game.

name: Accounting records
description: A clipped sheaf of ledger forms listing payments and purchases. Every column balances.
notes: Letter-size forms, 216 by 279 mm and 6 mm thick, three sheets a little out of square with rows of figures and a red heading on the top sheet, held by a black binder clip. The mass is the reference's 1 g, far lighter than a real sheaf of about 100 g. CHECK VOLUME (x820): the reference's 1 mL is a placeholder; flat paper of this size has a 0.4 L box. In the reference both ledgers belong to a trader quest; Deadvox has no such faction, so they stand as office finds. The falsified ledger has its own draft on this model.

name: Falsified accounting records
description: A clipped sheaf of ledger forms listing payments and purchases. The balances do not match, and a large sum is missing.
notes: Shares the accounting_records model: the two ledgers look the same and differ only in what reading them shows. It is a separate item rather than a variant because the reference keeps it as one, and its name tells the two apart. The mass and volume notes on accounting_records apply here.
